general.temas: The war in Ukraine and the US proposal on Donbas are recurring topics, as is the debate over German participation in the European GCAP fighter jet project. The rival demonstrations in Parma, bot messages directed at politicians and the fine imposed on Meta also feature. Only Corriere della Sera highlights the investigation into Giovanni Toti and his meetings with businessman Spinelli.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are high over the war in Ukraine and disagreements about possible terms for ending it. In Italy, the rival demonstrations in Parma, allegations involving political bots and the controversy over fascism reflect social and partisan polarization. Differences within the governing coalition over the Superbonus and suspicions surrounding the Ligurian government are also causing friction. Sports, technology and consumer news provide calmer subjects that partly offset this climate.

Corriere della Sera.resumen:
- The front page questions whether changes to the traffic code will reduce casualties.
- Several stories address meetings on a yacht and alleged irregularities in Liguria, including the manipulation of pandemic data; Genoa's mayor demands explanations and denies the allegations.
- A complaint has been filed against Fedez in the Iovino case, and he denies being present; Camila Giorgi faces tax proceedings.
- Disagreement within the governing coalition over the Superbonus and the tax on drinks is highlighted, alongside criticism of borrowing and advice on saving money.
- Russian troops are advancing toward Kharkiv; Zelensky acknowledges that the situation is very difficult.
Corriere della Sera.motivo_populismo: The coverage is predominantly factual, but expressions such as “the case erupts,” “attack” and “a game of massacre” emphasize conflict and dramatize some issues.
Corriere della Sera.sesgo: The selection prioritizes investigations and controversies affecting public officials, paying attention to their statements and defenses. It also takes a critical view of the traffic reform and borrowing, without displaying a clear partisan orientation.

la Repubblica.resumen:
- Zelensky outlines a US proposal on NATO and Donbas; Italy denies opposing Germany's participation in a European fighter jet project.
- A report links European rearmament to fears of Russia and highlights the future role of drones and artificial intelligence.
- Italy's privacy regulator fines Meta 805 million euros for using photos and videos without consent; the company will appeal.
- More than 20,000 people march in Parma against a far-right demonstration. Another report covers messages from suspicious accounts to Italian politicians.
- The front page addresses the risk that furniture subsidies will benefit upper-middle-income households, a dispute over the Ciro Grillo case and several sports stories.
la Repubblica.motivo_populismo: Factual headlines predominate, although expressions such as “the czar,” “fury” and “bot revolt” add drama, and some stories present confrontations through quoted statements.
la Repubblica.sesgo: The front page highlights the Russian threat and presents the Parma march as a civil society response to the far right. It also takes a critical view of furniture subsidies and the role of lobby groups.

La Stampa.resumen:
- Zelensky outlines a US proposal on Donbas and NATO; the coverage also includes demands attributed to Russia and Ukrainians' distrust of the negotiations.
- Italy opens the door to Germany joining the GCAP fighter jet program, while Farage calls Putin a threat to the United Kingdom.
- AI-generated messages reveal the presence of bots under political posts; a network outage disrupts Microsoft services.
- Sinner advises young people to stay away from social media, and several headlines highlight the impact of the ATP Finals in Turin.
- A communications failure causes thousands of flight cancellations in the United States; an analyst points to aging infrastructure.
La Stampa.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although expressions such as “chaos in the skies” and “fake negotiations” add drama; the latter is attributed to Ukrainian voices.
La Stampa.sesgo: The selection gives particular prominence to the war in Ukraine and includes perspectives critical of Russia, as well as a favorable assessment of tennis's impact on Turin. It also includes an analyst's explanation that is critical of US Republicans.

Il Giornale.resumen:
- Demonstration in Milan against the high cost of living and rearmament; searches in 13 cities.
- Controversy over La Russa's comments on fascism and criticism from the left.
- Ukraine debates a US proposal on Donbas and NATO; Italy denies reports about the GCAP program.
- News about a deadly scam involving fake police officers and investigations related to imams and polygamy.
- Meloni proposes raising the threshold for the simplified tax regime for self-employed workers to 100,000 euros; Meta receives an 805 million euro fine.
Il Giornale.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “they put him in the pillory,” “shock investigation” and “second-class self-employed workers for the left” combine dramatization, sensationalism and political confrontation.
Il Giornale.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach favorable to La Russa and Meloni and critical of the left. They also highlight crime stories and investigations involving Egyptian people and imams.

Il Fatto Quotidiano.resumen:
- A cyberattack on a subsidiary of the French postal service exposed the contact details of 22 million people.
- In Parma, an anti-fascist demonstration responded to a march for remigration; another story highlights the participation of a League councilor.
- A court upheld three life sentences in the Aemilia trial, and three people were arrested over labor exploitation in Prato.
- Biden criticizes Netanyahu in his memoirs; reports also cover a Russian decision against Zelensky and differences between Italy and Germany over a fighter jet project.
- The front page includes stories about measles in the United States, Virginia Raggi's possible candidacy, the artist Fabio Mauri and a scam suffered by Veronica Peparini.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.motivo_populismo: Some headlines rely on contrast and impact, such as the “twenty thousand anti-fascists” set against the “1,500” attendees at the other march, or the scam victim left with “4 euros.” However, factual wording predominates, without appeals to the people against the elites.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.sesgo: The front page pays particular attention to the anti-fascist mobilization and presents the remigration march critically, highlighting Roman salutes and chants in praise of Mussolini. The selection combines that political approach with international, judicial, health and cultural news.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I read the news through the lens of class struggle. In Prato, a worker's complaint has exposed twelve-hour days without breaks or holidays. This is not an anomaly that can be dismissed with indignation: when profit rules over labor, exploitation finds fertile ground. We need strong unions, inspections and real power for those who produce the wealth.

While billions are being discussed for a new European fighter jet, I would argue for investing in health care, education and public infrastructure. And in response to the penalty imposed on Meta for using photos and videos without consent, a fine is not enough: we need democratic control and collective ownership of essential platforms. In Parma, those who demonstrated against the far right remind us that solidarity among workers cannot stop at any border.
opiniones.anarquista:
I see more than a case of exploitation in the news from Prato: twelve-hour days without breaks or holidays show what happens when workers lack power against those in charge. It is not enough to wait for the state to punish wrongdoing afterward; we need autonomous organization, independent unions and mutual aid so that no one has to face those conditions alone.

In Parma, thousands of people have taken to the streets to reject remigration. There I recognize a different force: collective freedom exercised in the streets against a project of exclusion. I do not trust political parties to defend it for us. A free society is built from below, with communities capable of making decisions, welcoming and caring for one another without delegating their fate to political or economic hierarchies.
opiniones.liberal:
I see the same temptation in the debate over the tax on drinks and tax breaks for furniture: letting the state decide what we should consume and which sectors deserve support. I prefer low taxes and general rules. That way, families keep more of what they earn and businesses compete to satisfy them, not to secure privileges.

I also welcome the discussion of easing the burden on self-employed workers: anyone who risks their own money should be able to reap the rewards of their efforts. But freedom requires responsibility. Piling up debt without considering who will pay it passes today's decisions on to tomorrow's taxpayers. I want a limited state, capable of carrying out its functions without spending as though resources were inexhaustible.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I see more than a dispute over numbers in the Parma marches. Immigration is not an inevitable destiny: Italy has the right to decide who enters, who stays and under what conditions. I stand for strict borders, effective deportations of those who have no right to stay, and integration that requires respect for our laws and traditions. I will not accept the media elites turning that position into a taboo.

Sovereignty also requires security and a state worthy of trust. Suspicions about pandemic data in Liguria must be clarified without prejudice or impunity: if those in power manipulate information, they betray the citizens. And cooperation on the future European fighter jet will make sense only if it protects Italy's industrial capacity and freedom to make its own decisions. Italy's interests first.
opiniones.centro:
I see in the news proof that moderation is not indifference. The proposal that, according to Zelensky, the United States made to Ukraine on Donbas and NATO deserves an honest debate, but no peace will be legitimate if it is imposed on Ukrainians. I support negotiations and European security, without confusing the desire for an agreement with an obligation to accept any agreement.

In Parma, the mobilization against remigration shows the value of an active civil society. I defend the right to demonstrate and also reject proposals that turn entire groups into a problem. Living together requires strong institutions and rules that are equal for everyone. On the economy, I would review incentives for furniture and appliances if they mainly benefit middle- and high-income households: the market needs stable rules, and public spending must reach those who need it most.
